hints.junior: Every individual step in the agent's reasoning was right. The outcome wasn't, because nothing checked the plan before it ran.
hints.mid: Decide and execute being the same step means every planning mistake becomes a production mistake, instantly.
hints.staff: Same reason human deploys have had review-then-execute for decades: the cost of an irreversible action justifies a cheap gate.

hints.junior: Same proposed action, two paths, toggle between it running instantly and it waiting for your click.
hints.mid: The pending state shows the real parameters, not a paraphrase, that's what makes the approval meaningful.
hints.staff: Reject is a first-class outcome here, not just withheld approval, it explicitly cancels the queued action.

hints.junior: The tool call becomes a proposal shown to a human first. Nothing runs until someone clicks Approve.
hints.mid: The tool's interface stays the same, what changes is it enqueues instead of executing, pending an explicit approval event.
hints.staff: Show the actual parameters, not a summary, approving a paraphrase isn't approving the action.

hints.junior: A vague approval prompt turns the gate into a formality. Always show the specific, real details.
hints.mid: Add a timeout to pending actions, a stale approval on now-outdated data shouldn't still be one click from executing.
hints.staff: Log who approved what parameters, that's the audit trail that matters after an incident, not the agent's reasoning trace.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about an agent that decided on a production action and executed it in the very same step, with nobody able to catch a mistake in between.
sections.mid: Giving an agent tool access to production-affecting actions with no review step means every mistake in its plan becomes a mistake in production instantly, with no chance to catch it.
sections.staff: This isn't primarily an AI-safety framing — it's the same reason production deploys have had a review-then-execute step for humans for decades.

sections.junior: The fix is separating proposing an action from executing it, so the agent's plan sits in a pending state until a human explicitly approves it.
sections.mid: The tool's interface stays the same, but instead of executing, it enqueues the action with its full parameters and returns a pending state until a human explicitly approves.
sections.staff: The gate needs to show the actual parameters the action will run with, not a paraphrase — approving a summary isn't approving the action.

sections.junior: Compare an action that runs the moment the agent decides on it against one that waits for your explicit approval or rejection.
sections.mid: The pending state shows the real parameters, not a summary, which is exactly what makes the approval meaningful.
sections.staff: Reject is a real, first-class outcome here, not just "don't click approve" — it explicitly cancels the queued action.

sections.junior: Anything with real production side effects needs a review step before it runs, not just good reasoning behind it.
sections.mid: Separate proposing an action from executing it — show the real parameters, and require an explicit approval click before anything runs.
sections.staff: Reserve the gate for genuinely high-blast-radius actions — gating everything trains reviewers to rubber-stamp instead of actually reading.
